extracted.intended_audience: early-career investigators applying for NIH K01 career development awards in global health/infectious disease (reviewers and program officers are secondary audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A mentored K01 career development application describing candidate goals, specific aims (geospatial + transmission modeling of HIV-TB), training/mentoring plan, timeline, and pathway to independence aimed at producing R01-competitive research and stakeholder-engaged implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected research effort requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This K01 award will support me to devote at least 75% of my effort to research as I develop techniques ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department of Global Health has committed to protecting at least 75% of my time for research activities. Non-research time: clinical practice up to 4 weeks/year (≤6%); teaching responsibilities <6%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development goal alignment / research niche
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term career goal is to be an academic investigator focused on applying geospatial and modeling methods to support targeted interventions to address HIV and co-infections in sub-Saharan Africa; work at the intersection of modeling and implementation science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K01 period goals should position candidate to apply geographic information about infectious disease burden to inform clinical intervention programs and future R01 proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete short-term K01 objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term goals for K01 award period include learning geospatial modeling techniques; designing, constructing, and validating mathematical models of HIV-TB co-infection; learning data visualization and implementation science; refining scientific writing and presentation skills; and successfully competing for R01 funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each short-term goal is linked to training activities (mentorship, coursework, tutorials, fieldwork, manuscript preparation) and to deliverables (manuscripts, presentations, R01 submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship plan and mentor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary mentor (Dr. Barnabas) and co-mentors with relevant expertise will provide mentoring; mentor qualifications include prior DPhil in mathematical modeling, >59 peer-reviewed publications, PI on funded grants, and prior mentees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify mentor expertise, history of mentorship, funded projects, frequency of interactions (e.g., weekly in-person with primary mentor; bi-weekly Skype with co-mentor; monthly meetings with other co-mentors), and concrete mentoring roles tied to aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinary team composition aligned to aims
rubrics_metrics.description: A large mentoring team (primary mentor, three co-mentors, scientific advisors) is necessary to complete multidisciplinary aims; Table 1 lists team members, roles, expertise, and meeting frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map each team member’s expertise to specific aims (e.g., geospatial modeling, transmission modeling, implementation science, TB surveillance interpretation) and state planned meeting cadence (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training activities (coursework, tutorials, fieldwork, conferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training will be achieved through didactic coursework, mentored field work, tutorials (hands-on mentoring), and attendance at conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a multi-year schedule showing which courses and activities are taken when (examples given: BIOST 555; EPI 554; SISMID; GH 590; GH 590c; GH 541; EPI 588; manuscript preparation short-course), include field time in Uganda and tutorials with mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathway to independence and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities to ensure on track to submit an R01 in year 4 include attending the UW ITHS Faculty Career Development Series, producing publications, and grant-writing training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify measurable milestones (e.g., produce at least 2 first-author manuscripts per year; take EPI 588: Writing Research Proposals in year 2; submit smaller proposals such as New Investigator Award; R01 preparation, submission and re-submission schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims must state approach and hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Specific Aim should include a clear Aim statement, an Approach summary, and an explicit Hypothesis (examples provided for Aim 1, Aim 2, Aim 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format mirrors provided examples: Aim heading, ‘Approach:’ paragraph, and ‘Hypothesis:’ sentence. Aims should be testable and tied to data/methods described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked geospatial and mathematical modeling strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop cutting-edge, linked geospatial and mathematical models to guide implementation at a sub-national (district) scale for preventive therapy (PT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy entails building district-level geospatial models of prevalence/incidence/mortality and then fitting a dynamic transmission model per district, parameterized using geospatial outputs; use same model structure across districts with region-specific parameter values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement integrated into model development
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage stakeholders to inform model development and evaluate strategies to improve acceptability and feasibility of modeled strategies for TB prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured interviews with HIV and TB stakeholders, assess how interactive model engagement affects acceptability and feasibility, and incorporate stakeholder feedback into model and dissemination plans (Aim 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple data sources and triangulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes and predictors should be derived from multiple data sources and triangulated (e.g., DHIS-2 TB mortality 2012–2017; 2014–2015 national TB prevalence survey; TB case notifications adjusted for underreporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify start years (e.g., 2012 when TB mortality included in DHIS-2), describe adjustments for under-ascertainment, and triangulate incidence estimates from prevalence and mortality via transmission model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictor selection and district-level aggregation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate predictor variables include TB prevalence, district HIV prevalence, district ART coverage, distance to health facility, presence of smear/Xpert, population density, undernutrition, poverty, etc.; for variables that vary across the district use population-weighted mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify data sources and types for each predictor (e.g., population-based survey; Bayesian hierarchical geostatistical model; aggregated patient data) and describe method to compute district-level values (population-weighting, mapping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling spatial dependence and district similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Geospatial model should incorporate the notion that adjacent districts may be more similar than geographically disparate ones (spatial autocorrelation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for spatial correlation in geostatistical modeling and justify model choices; use representative publications/methods as references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic review to inform efficacy parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a systematic review of the impact of PT on incident TB, TB mortality, and adverse effects among PLHIV and apply efficacy estimates to the mathematical model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pooled/stratified efficacy estimates from the review as model inputs and report uncertainties propagated into modeled outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness and regionalized implementation comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the cost of providing PT in health facilities or communities and quantify differences in TB outcomes and cost for regionalized PT implementation versus uniform rollout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model DALYs averted, cases and deaths averted, adverse effects, and programmatic cost; compare prioritized district-based scale-up to uniform strategies under same total cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling incidence estimation challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that incidence is the most challenging outcome to estimate; adjust case notifications for underreporting using maps of treatment-seeking behavior and TB diagnostic capacity and triangulate with transmission model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document adjustment methods and sensitivity analyses; report uncertainty in incidence estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary studies and evidence of feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide preliminary investigations demonstrating experience with geospatial modeling, TB burden modeling, mapping ART scale-up, and prior relevant contributions (e.g., manuscript under review, GBD work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how prior work supports ability to adapt methods to new data sources (e.g., using program surveillance instead of vital registration) and cite representative prior analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and scalability justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that proposed methods are innovative (linked geospatial + transmission models at sub-national scale; stakeholder engagement) and are scalable to other countries using routinely collected surveillance and demographic data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the project in context of policy/priorities (PEPFAR, NIH PA-15-010), reference analogous precedent (global malaria map) and propose generalizability to other sub-Saharan countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training timeline and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed multi-year components matrix showing which coursework, fieldwork, tutorials, and conferences will be taken each year (Pre-award/Year1–4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete course codes and names (BIOST 555; EPI 554; SISMID; GH 590; GH 541; GH 590c; EPI 588), planned tutorials with mentors, and timing of R01 preparation and submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with national programs and data access commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate letters of support and ongoing relationships with national programs (e.g., NTLP) to obtain necessary surveillance and program data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what data are public vs require permissions; explain how relationships will facilitate access and interpretation of surveillance data and stakeholder engagement.
